en: The Twenty-Verse Praise of the Wheel of the Blessed Lord Śrī Hevajra (Cakraviṃśatikāstotra).
Oṃ. Homage to Śrī Hevajra!
I prostrate to Hevajra, the Hero, who is the supreme nature of all phenomena, the primordial one abiding within the self of all, the non-duality of wisdom and means. (1)
With devotion, I bow to that Lord, whose neck is embraced by Nairātmyā;
whose tawny hair blazes upward; who has eight faces, each with three eyes. (2)
I bow to him whose roots are above, who is white and black, and whose right and left [faces] are white and red; all his remaining faces are black. (3)
[He is] endowed with eight skulls held in his eight right hands, which contain an elephant, a horse, a donkey, a cow, a camel, a man, a dog, and a buffalo. ||4||
I bow to him who holds in the skull-cups situated in his eight left hands the earth, water, wind, fire, the moon, the sun, Yama, and the Guhyakas.
I bow to him who has trampled the four Māras, who is clothed only by the directions with his four feet, who stands with the sun upon his upraised foot, who is blue in color, and who is dancing. (6)
It consists of four wheels, adorned with terrifying, dripping severed heads, and is beautifully decorated with mudrās representing the purity of the Tathāgatas. ||7||
I bow to that Great Bliss, who is marked on his head with a universal vajra, whose crown is adorned by the Lord of the Family, and who has attained supreme bliss. (8)
In the east, I bow to Gaurī, born from the syllable Gaṃ, whose body is black and whose left side is red; she holds a curved knife in her right hand and stands treading upon Brahmā. 9.
I bow to Caurī, who originates from the syllable Caṃ, who has the hue of madder, who holds a boar and a ḍamaru in her hands, and who is mounted upon Indra. 10.
I bow to that yellow Vetālī, born from the syllable *vaṃ*, who dwells with Upendra;
she holds a bowl in her left hand and a tortoise in her right. ||11||
I bow to Ghasmarī at the northern gate, who is dark green in color, born from the syllable *Ghaṃ*, holding a skull and a snake in her hands, and mounted upon Rudra. (12)
I bow to the blue Pukkasī, who stands upon Yama, is born from semen, holds an axe in her right hand, rides a lion, and possesses a terrifying form in the northeast. (13)
I bow to Śabarī, born from the syllable Śaṃ, white in color, situated in the southeast where Kubera resides;
she holds a rattle-drum in her left hand and a water-pot in her right. 14.
I bow to Caṇḍālī, who is dark as the sky, born from the letter *caṃ* in the southwest, who holds a plow in her right hand and a discus in her left, and who is the destroyer of the Rākṣasas. 15.
I bow to Ḍombī, born from the syllable *ḍaṃ*, who dwells in the northwest with Vemacitrin, who holds a threatening gesture and a vajra in her hands, and who has a variegated luster. (16)
Standing in the half-lotus dance posture, adorned with the five mudrās, all naked and three-eyed—I bow down to them all with devotion. (17)
Pure in their aggregates and elements, arisen from the thought of awakening—I bow with my whole being to all these who bestow happiness. (18)
I always pay perfect homage to all those who, having emerged from the seed-syllables and emblems attached to their own right arms, are ever devoted to great bliss. 19.
He who, possessing the sciences, was born from the pair of seeds situated within the vessel of the moon and sun;
that Lord, having fashioned these three worlds in the form of his own mandala by means of skillful method,
has withdrawn all this entire universe and the science that bestows true happiness into himself.
But he who is dissolved in his own state, which is the nectar-essence of the passion for wisdom—to him, homage! ||20||
Having praised Hevajra, the lord of ḍākinīs, together with the circle of goddesses,
by whatever merit I have acquired through this, may the world become equal to him.
The *Cakraviṃśikā-stotra* to the Lord Śrī Hevajra is completed.
This work is the composition of the accomplished master Sauroruhapāda.
